flags.purpose: Filter routes by destination prefix to identify specific routes including the default gateway.
flags.security_use_case: Identify the default gateway and primary egress path used for outbound traffic.
flags.threat_detected: Unexpected default gateway indicating route hijacking, VPN redirection, or rogue DHCP influence.
flags.detection_pattern: DestinationPrefix = 0.0.0.0/0 AND NextHop not in baseline list.
flags.forensic_value: Shows which gateway the system used during incident timeframe for internet-bound traffic.
flags.baseline_value: Default gateway and interface should match known network design.
flags.safe_followup: Validate gateway MAC with Get-NetNeighbor; compare against baseline.

flags.purpose: Filter routes bound to a specific network interface.
flags.security_use_case: Audit routing table for multi-homed hosts and detect unexpected routing via secondary adapters.
flags.threat_detected: Routes present on unexpected adapters (e.g., Wi-Fi, VPN, virtual NIC).
flags.detection_pattern: InterfaceAlias not in approved adapters list.
flags.forensic_value: Indicates which adapter carried suspicious traffic.
flags.baseline_value: Critical routes should exist only on approved primary adapters.
flags.safe_followup: Validate adapters with Get-NetAdapter; review VPN/virtual NIC software.

flags.purpose: Filter routes by the protocol that installed them (Local, NetMgmt, DHCP, RIP, OSPF, BGP, etc.).
flags.security_use_case: Detect routes injected by DHCP or dynamic routing protocols.
flags.threat_detected: Routes added by rogue DHCP or unauthorized routing daemons.
flags.detection_pattern: Protocol = DHCP AND NextHop not trusted.
flags.forensic_value: Attribution of how malicious route entered the routing table.
flags.baseline_value: Most endpoints should only have Local/NetMgmt routes unless routing is intentional.
flags.safe_followup: Inspect DHCP server; check for rogue network devices.

flags.purpose: View routing table for IPv4 or IPv6 specifically.
flags.security_use_case: Audit IPv6 routes which may bypass IPv4-focused monitoring controls.
flags.threat_detected: Unexpected IPv6 routes enabling covert communication or lateral movement.
flags.detection_pattern: AddressFamily = IPv6 AND DestinationPrefix not link-local/ULA/multicast.
flags.forensic_value: Reveals hidden IPv6 communication paths used during compromise.
flags.baseline_value: IPv6 routes should be documented or IPv6 disabled if unused.
flags.safe_followup: Review IPv6 firewall coverage; disable IPv6 if unnecessary.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Correlates default gateway IP with ARP/MAC to detect ARP spoofing or man-in-the-middle.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Validate gateway identity during suspected network interception.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Shows all active routes currently used for traffic forwarding.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Identify live routing paths during incident response.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Finds default routes installed via DHCP which may indicate rogue DHCP attack.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detect attacker-controlled DHCP altering victim routing behavior.
